analysis.text:
As an early-entry candidate, the consensus No. 1 overall pick would follow Kwame Brown as the second prep player to be chosen first in the draft. Named USA Today's high school basketball player of the year, James was also the recipient of the Gatorade Award, presented annually to the nation's top high school player, and a member of the McDonald's All-American team.

Averaged 30.4 points, 9.7 rebounds, 4.9 assists and 2.9 steals while leading team to No. 1 national ranking, fourth straight state tournament and third state title. James became the first three-time Ohio Mr. Basketball winner, leading SMSV to the 2003 Division II state title after guiding Irish to Division III title as freshman and sophomore. Lost in Division II final as junior.

James was named MVP of the McDonald's High School all-star game, the Jordan Capital Classic and the EA Sports Roundball Classic.

Controversy surrounded James this past season, however, as he was declared ineligible by the Ohio High School Athletic Association in January after admitting he accepted $845 in "throwback'' jerseys. James, however, was cleared of allegations he violated amateur bylaws by accepting a Hummer H2 vehicle as a gift. He won a court order in February allowing him to complete his senior year.

At just 17, Darko is Europe's version of LeBron James. He's comfortable on the perimeter and with his back to the basket. He's very aggressive in the post and has a toughness many Europeans lack. He can also handle, shoot the 3 and play in the paint. He has a nasty streak that have some scouts calling him a tough version of Raef LaFrentz.

He struggled two weeks ago in front a packed house of NBA scouts in Greece. He gets into foul trouble, limiting his court time.  He still lacks consistency.  One night he's huge, the next night he disappears.

Notes: Milicic is a 17-year-old left-handed power forward who was born in the former Yugoslavia, today known as Serbia. He is currently playing for a professional team, KK Hemofarm, in Versac, Serbia. Milicic became a professional player at age 16. Milicic is currently averaging 13 points, eight rebounds and shooting 59 percent from the field.

Milicic is considered one of the most versatile young players in basketball for his ability to shoot from the outside and still dominate in the paint. He can dunk in traffic, shoot NBA threes and is a formidable shot blocking defender.

Just about every team in the NBA has traveled to Yugoslavia to see him play. They all came away impressed. It isn't very often that you find a big man with the type of skills he possesses. He's as fundamentally sound as anyone in the draft. He'll be a top three pick in this year's draft.

An early-entry candidate, Anthony played just a single season at Syracuse, but packed a career's worth of highlights in freshman season. He was named second team All-America by The Associated Press as a freshman after leading Syracuse to a 30-5 record and the school's first NCAA championship in men's basketball. Named Most Valuable Player of the 2003 NCAA Final Four and MVP of NCAA East Regional.

Anthony was a consensus national Freshman of the Year. He was the unanimous choice as Big East Conference Freshman of the Year and was an All-Big East First Team selection. Named Big East Rookie of the Week a league-record 10 times.

Averaged 22.2 points (16th in nation, 4th in Big East) and 10.0 rebounds (19th in nation, 3rd in Big East). Posted 22 double-doubles and led team in scoring in 24 of 35 games. Led team in scoring, rebounding, minutes played (36.4 mpg), field goals made and attempted and free throws made and attempted. Was second on the team to fellow freshman Gerry McNamara in assists (2.2 apg) and steals (1.57 spg) and in three-pointers made and attempted.

In the national championship game victory over Kansas, Anthony scored 20 points, added 10 rebounds and dished out seven assists. In Final Four win over Texas, exploded for a season-high 33 points and 14 rebounds. In six NCAA Tournament games, averaged 20.2 points and 9.8 rebounds.

Scored at least 20 points in 25 of 35 games. Played 38 or more minutes in 16 games and played at least 30 minutes in all but one game. Notched career-high 15 rebounds twice, vs. Georgetown and Connecticut. Also grabbed 14 rebounds four times. Produced 27 points and 11 rebounds in collegiate debut vs. Memphis. Recorded 30-point outings vs. Rutgers and at Georgetown. Hit 10-for-10 from the line against both Notre Dame and Rutgers.

As a high school senior, led Oak Hill Academy to a 32-1 record and a No. 3 final national ranking in USA Today. Averaged 21.7 points and 7.4 rebounds. Named First Team All-America by USA Today and PARADE and was named to the McDonald's All-America Team. In the McDonald's All-America Game, scored 19 points to help the East to victory.

An early-entry candidate, Bosh was the ACC's Rookie of the Year and a second-team all-Atlantic Coast Conference selection after leading Tech in scoring and rebounding. Bosh ranked eighth in the conference in scoring (15.6 ppg) and second in rebounding (9.0 rpg). He also ranked first in the ACC field goal percentage (56.0) and blocked shots (2.16 per game).

The Lancaster, Texas, native led team with 18.0 points and 9.3 rebounds while shooting 58.1 percent from the floor in three NIT games. He recorded double figures in both points and rebounds 13 times during the season.

The only freshman to make either the first or second all-ACC team, Bosh also made the national all-freshman team chosen by the United States Basketball Writers Association, which also named Bosh to its all-South region team. Bosh also was named to the all-District 5 team by the National Association of Basketball Coaches.

An early-entry candidate, Wade became the most decorated player in Marquette history in just two seasons. His 1,281 career points is 20th on the school's all-time scoring list and he recorded a career 19.7 points per game scoring average, good for the No. 2 spot all-time at Marquette. Other career categories where he ranked prominently included steals (9th, 150) and blocked shots (9th, 79). Scored in double figures in 62 of his 65 career contests.

During the 2002-03 season, Wade became the first Marquette player since 1978 to earn first-team honors on the Associated Press All-America Team and helped Marquette reach the Final Four for the first time since 1979. Wade was also named USBWA First Team All-America and NABC Second Team All-America.

Wade was Conference USA's player of the year after leading the team and the league in scoring in both overall (21.5 ppg) and conference contests (20.4 ppg). Wade was also named C-USA defensive player of the year, while earning selection to the Wooden Award All-American Team as one of five finalists for the coveted honor.

Wade ranked No. 10 among C-USA players in field goal percentage (.501), tied for No. 11 with teammate Robert Jackson in free throw percentage (.779), No. 8 in assists (4.39 apg) and No. 2 in steals (2.15 spg). Established a school seasonal scoring record in 2002-03 with 710 points, bettering the previous mark of 689 held by Tony Smith (1989-90). Wade also came up with Marquette's first triple-double since 1994 when he totaled 29 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists in leading the Golden Eagles to an 83-69 win over No. 1-ranked Kentucky in the NCAA Midwest Regional Final -- where he was named the Midwest Regional Outstanding Player after compiling 51 points, 14 rebounds and 15 assists in wins over Pittsburgh and Kentucky.

The early-entry candidate leaves Central Michigan as its seventh-leading career rebounder with 707 boards and 11th-leading scorer with 1,250 points. Kaman holds the CMU career field goal percentage record at 60.8 percent, and one of only players in CMU's 1,000-point, 600-rebound club.

Kaman was named a Associated Press honorable mention All-America. He was the Mid-American Conference's Player of the Year and Defensive Player of the Year -- as well as the MAC tournament MVP. He was tirst team All-MAC and USBWA All-District, while being selected to the NABC second team All-District.

Kaman led the nation in double-doubles (25) and ranked fourth nationally in rebounding (12.0), sixth in field goal percentage (62.2), 10th in blocked shots (3.2) and 13th in scoring (22.4). He Central Michigan to the MAC regular season and tournament titles and the second round of the NCAA Tournament.

Kaman was also one of only five players nationally to average at least 20 points and 10 rebounds in 2002-03 (Brandon Hunter, Ohio; David West, Xavier; Mike Sweetney, Georgetown; Carmelo Anthony, Syracuse). He led the MAC in field goal percentage and blocks, while ranking second in scoring and rebounding. Kaman scored a career-high 43 points against Ball State this past season and set CMU single-season records for blocks (98) and rebounds (373).

Perhaps the most athletic player in Europe at the moment, Pietrus has a very American game. He can take it to the basket and shoot the NBA 3. He's aggressive on both ends of the court. He's very strong for his size. He also has a nice shooting touch.
Still needs to work on his ball-handling.  He has the ability to take his man one-on-one, but because of the style of game his team plays, he rarely gets the opportunity to.

Pietrus, 20, has played for EB Pau-Orthez (France) since 1999. Averaged 9.4 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.6 assists in the ProA regular season. Pietrus was a member of the 2000-01 French National Championship with EB Pau Orthez. Won the 2002 and 2003 French National Cup with EB Pau Orthez.

Pietrus has been member of the French Junior National Team, winning the gold medal at the 2000 European Junior Championship. Has been a member of the French Under-20 National Teamm which won the silver medal at the 2002 European Under-20 Championship.

Think a mixture of Desmond Mason and Ricky Davis (without the attitude). The Bulls have already been making numerous inquiries. He could go as high as No.7. He probably won't slip past the Grizzlies at No. 13.

Hinrich helped Kansas reach back-to-back Final Fours as junior and senior, earning All-Final Four Team honors this year. He was an AP Third-Team All-American; named to the John R. Wooden All-American Team; and named NCAA Tournament West Region Most Outstanding Player.

Hinrich was a First-Team All-Big 12 (AP and Coaches) selection, as well as a member of the Big 12 All-Defense Team. Hinrich was a Naismith Award Top 20 Finalist and named to the Wooden Award Midseason Top 30. Prior t his senior season, Hinricha was named to the Associated Press Preseason All-American Team.

Hinrich started all 37 games in which he played (sat out one game due to a back strain) as a senior and ranked second on the team with a career-high 17.3 points per game (good for fourth in the Big 12) on 47.5 percent shooting from the field. Hinrich nailed a team-high 89 three-pointers, and shot 40.6 percent from beyond the arc. Hinrich ranked second on the squad and 10th in the Big 12 with 3.5 assists per contest, while grabbing 3.8 boards and tallying 1.9 steals per game.

He led KU in scoring 16 times and in assists on six occasions. Hinrich poured in a career-high 29 points -- including a career-best seven three-pointers against UMKC -- on Jan. 4.

The early-entry candidate was of the top players in Texas history. A two-year starter at point guard for the Longhorns, Ford led Texas to the Sweet 16 as a freshman, before guiding the Horns to their first Final Four appearance since 1947 during his sophomore campaign of 2002-03.

For his efforts, Ford earned National Player of the Year accolades by several media entities as a sophomore. Winner of the Naismith and Wooden Awards as the top player in college basketball. Ford was also named National Player of the Year by several media agencies (Sports Illustrated, ESPN.com, CBS SportsLine, The Sporting News). Ford was a consensus first-team All-America choice and selected to the NABC District 9 first-team for the second straight season after being a first-team All-Big 12 pick (by league?s coaches and media)

Ford rests in second place on UT?s all-time career assists list (527) and holds the top two single-season assists marks in school history (273 in 2001-02; 254 in 2002-03). He led the team in scoring (15.0 ppg), assists (7.70 apg), steals (2.00 spg), free throw percentage (.820) and minutes (33.6 mpg) as a sophomore -- after becoming the first freshman in NCAA history to lead the nation in assists (8.27 apg).

Ford posted nine double-digit assist performances on the year and recorded 111 assists against just 40 turnovers during Big 12 Conference play.

Voted National Freshman of the Year by the USBWA (United States Basketball Writers Association), CNNSI.com and CollegeInsider.com in 2001-02.

West became Xavier's first National Player of the Year when he won the 2002-03 Rupp Trophy, which is the award given by the Associated Press its top college player. West also won the 2002-03 Oscar Robertson Player of the Year Trophy, which is the National Player of the Year award for the USBWA (U.S. Basketball Writers Association). West was also named as the 2002-03 Basketball Times Player of the Year and finished second in the balloting for the John R. Wooden Award for player of the year.

West was named as a 2002-03 First Team All-American by the Associated Press, the USBWA, the NABC (National Association of Basketball Coaches) and the John R. Wooden Award. He was the first player in Xavier history to be named to the first team of a major All-American team and was also the recipient of the 2002-03 NABC/Pete Newell Big Man of the Year Award, which is presented annually during the National Association of Basketball Coaches Convention at the Final Four.

West was the first player to win three A-10 Player of the Year awards, having earned them in each of his last three years. He also was named to the A-10 All-Defensive Team for the third straight year in 2003.

As can be expected, West set numerous records during his four seasons at Xavier. West finished with 2,132 career points and grabbed 1,308 career rebounds. Only four players have reached the 2,000-point, 1,000-rebound plateau over the last six years: West, Raef LaFrentz (Kansas ?98), Nick Collison (Kansas ?03) and Brandon Hunter (Ohio ?03). Xavier has only one other player in its history that has collected over 2,000 points and 1,000 rebounds: Tyrone Hill (1986-90) had 2,003 points and a school record 1,380 rebounds.

West was among the top five in almost every category in the Atlantic Ten: points (20.1 ppg, third), rebounding (11.8 rpg, first), field goal percentage (51.3 percent, second), free throw percentage (81.6 percent, third) and blocked shots (1.6 bpg, fourth). West tallied a school record 68 career ?double-doubles? in scoring-rebounding during his career, and had 22 double-doubles as a senior, including his 47-point, 18-rebound game against Dayton; his 25-point, 14-rebound game at Saint Joseph?s; a 28-point, 11-rebound game against Creighton, and a 20-point, 12-rebound game at Richmond.

West scored in double figures 110 times in his career and 86 of the last 87 games in his career with the only non-double figure game during that 85-game stretch being the injury-shortened nine-point game against Cincinnati on December 14, 2001. In fact, West scored in double figures in each of his last 56 games, which is the second longest streak in Xavier history. West also broke two other career school records with his 662 free throws made and 874 free throws attempted.

A big-time prospect who's been overshadowed by the emergence of teammate Mickael Pietrus. He's very smooth and one of the best passers ESPN.com has seen in the draft. He has a real point guard mentality and is very unselfish. He has a nice body and is a good athlete. Diaw was the French League's MVP this season.

The only question with Diaw is aggressiveness. He can be too passive on the offensive end of the court. He just rarely looks for his shot. Some scouts believe that will change when Diaw gets out of the system he's playing in and gets more familiar with the NBA.

A member of Pau Orthez (France) since 2000-01 season, Diaw averaged 5.8 points, 4.7 rebounds and 3.0 assists this past season. Made made his debut during the 1997-98 season with JSA Bordeaux, in the French 4th division. In 1998-99 moved to INSEP, the French National Institute for Sports, in the French National 1 League, the French 3rd division. Also played with INSEP during the 1999-2000 championships.

Diaw was part of the 2002 and 2003 French National Cup with EB Pau Orthez, while also being named to the 2002 French All Star Game. He won the silver medal at the 2002 European Under-20 Championship. Also won the 2000-01 French National Championship with EB Pau Orthez. He was a member of the French Junior National team, which won the gold medal at the 2000 European Championship, as well as the French Under-20 National team. Diaw played at the 2000 European Under-20 Championships.

He's really a 6-foot-9 pass-first old school point guard. He'll never average more than 12 to 15 ppg in the league, but he'll get you five or six rebounds and five or six assists per game. He's probably a mid-to-late first-rounder.

Howard was named the national player of the year by Fox, Basketball Digest and College Insider. Also named first team All-American by the National Association of Basketball Coaches. He was a finalist for the John R. Wooden and Naismith Awards and was a unanimous selection for 2003 ACC Player of the Year honors -- the first player to earn unanimous honors since David Thompson in 1975.

Wake's first All-American and first ACC Player of the Year since Tim Duncan in 1997, Howard was the leading vote-getter for the ACC All-Defense Team. Joins Shane Battier as the only players in the history of the ACC to accumulate 1,000 points, 500 rebounds, 200 assists, 200 steals, 100 blocked shots and 100 three-point field goals.

Howard leaves Wake ranked second in career steals (215), third in games started, fifth in blocked shots, sixth in double-doubles (22), sixth in games played, seventh in rebounding, eighth in three-point attempts, 10th in scoring, and 10th in three-point field goals made. As a senior, Howard led the ACC in scoring and ranked in the top 10 in seven other statistical categories.

Howard led Wake Forest to the 2002-03 ACC regular season championship -- its first outright title in 41 years. Led Wake Forest to a 87-44 record during his four-year career and three consecutive NCAA Tournament appearances.

The early-entry candidate was a first team all-Big East selection after leading the Hoyas in scoring (22.8), rebounding (10.4), blocks (3.2), field goals (264), field goal percentage (.547), free throws (248) and free throw attempts (336). Sweetney was also selected to the NABC All-American second team and was a finalist for the Naismith Award. Sweetney was also a Wooden Award candidate and Associated Press All-American (Honorable Mention).

Sweetney had 16 double-doubles as a junior, bringing his career total to 38. Scored a career-high 38 points at Notre Dame and led the team in scoring in 24 of 34 games, while leading Georgetown in rebounding in 29 of 34 games.

As a junior, Sweetney was the USBWA District II Player of the Year and first team All Big East selection. He is a two time Playboy All-American.

An early-entry candidate, half of the "Luke & Luke Show" will likely be the second point guard picked in the draft. Whether that means he's a lottery pick depends on how well he plays over the next month in Chicago and at individual workouts.

The 2003 Pac-10 player of the year and MVP of the conference tournament, Ridnour was an honorable mention AP All-America after setting an Oregon record for assists in a season with 218 and tying another school record with 63 steals. Ridnour leaves Oregon as its third-leading assists man with 500, second in steals with 150, and third in 3-pointers with 203.

Ridnour was also named to the Basketball Times, NABC and USBWA all-district first teams. As a sophomore, Ridnour was an honorable mention All-America selection by AP, as well as first team All-Pac-10 selection. Ridnour started all 96 games in his Oregon career and leaves as the school's second-best career free throw shooter (85.9 percent) and ranks eighth in three-point shooting at 38.9 percent. He set a Pac-10 record for consecutive free throws made (62) and led the Pac-10 in assists (6.6 apg) and free throw shooting (88 percent) as a junior.

Ridnour was the Pac-10's second-leading scorer in 2002-03 (19.7 ppg), which also ranked eighth all-time on OU's single-season list. He led Oregon in scoring, assists, steals, free throw shooting and minutes. He was one of only three Pac-10 players to score in double figures in each game this past season.

An early-entry candidate, Perkins was a three time All-State and All-Region selection out of Clifton J. Ozen High School in Texas, and led Clifton to four consecutive District Championships, one State Championship and a 96-3 record over the past three seasons.

Perkins has not yet signed with an agent. He will withdraw his name and attend the University of Memphis if he's not satisfied with his NBA options.

But whether it's on the college or professional level, Kendrick is the definition of a low post player. He has a power game that consists of drop steps and up-and-under moves. Perkins uses his size to his advantage as he is a solid rebounder and defender. For a big man he has soft hands and can catch almost anything thrown to him.

Collison was instrumental is Kansas' back-to-back appearances in the Final Four. He was named to the NCAA All-Final Four Team as the Jayhawks lost to Syracuse in the national championship game -- a game that saw Collison score 19 points and grab 21 rebounds.

The NABC National Player of the Year and AP First-Team All-American was also named to the John R. Wooden All-American Team, NCAA Tournament West Region All-Tournament Team and Basketball Times First-Team All-American Team. Other honors included USBWA First- Team All-American; Big 12 Player of the Year (Coaches); NABC First-Team All-American; First-Team All-Big 12 (AP and Coaches) and Naismith Award Top 20 Finalist. Collison was also a Preseason First Team All-Big 12 (Coaches) and Playboy Preseason All-American.

As a senior, Collison Started all 38 games, averaging team-highs of 18.5 points and 10.0 rebounds per contest. He ranked second in the Big 12 in scoring and third in rebounding. His 702 points on the year rank seventh in a single-season in KU history.

Collison shot 55.4 percent from the field and nailed a career-high 13 three-pointers. He dished out 84 assists and racked up a team-high 1.9 blocks per game. Collison also posted a team-high 16 double-doubles, leading the Jayhawks in scoring 14 times and in rebounding 21 times.

Collison poured in a career-high 33 points against Duke on March 27 in the Sweet 16. He ripped down a career-best 23 rebounds versus Texas on Big Monday on Jan. 27 -- the most rebounds by any KU player under coach Roy Williams.

Considered one of the top three young players in Europe right now, Lampe's combination of size, shooting touch, ball-handling skills and an advanced inside-outside games have drawn comparisons to Dirk Nowitzki. His shooting stroke is one of the smoothest we've ever seen in a big kid. He's got a nice body, has a very fluid game, and despite reports to the contrary, looked very good with his back to the basket when ESPN.com saw him play in Spain in May.

He's not a great rebounder and some teams are concerned with his aggressiveness.  He spends too much time hanging around the perimeter for a 7-footer.  He's not the athlete that Nowitzki is nor does have the strength necessary to play in the post. He's a bit of a tweener.  He has the size of a four, but the mentality of a three.

Having just turned 18 years old, Lampe is a native of Lodz, Poland, is currently affiliated with Real Madrid in Spain. Fluent in six languages, Lampe is one of the most exciting young athletes in the world. Lampe should become the first Poland-born player to be drafted into the NBA.

At 15, Lampe moved to Sweden and began playing professionally for Alvik Stockholm. He split time between Alvik Stockholm and Polish Junior National Team. And after his first season, Lampe was purchased by Real Madrid.

In January, 2002 he was invited to play in the 23rd Annual International Tournament of Ciutat de Hospitalitat, a tournament that boasts the best 16 and 17-year-old basketball European players. He finished the tournament as the leading scorer. That same year, Lampe played in the European Championships for Junior National Players in Germany, where he solidified his reputation as one of the top Junior players in Europe.

Lampe could be the sleeper of the draft.  He has most of the intagibles teams look for in a big guy.  He won't have an immediate impact in the league, but at 18, he has time to develop.  In two or three years, watch out.

An early-entry candidate, Outlaw averaged 25 points, 10 rebounds and six blocked shots a game at Starkville High School, guiding the Yellow Jackets to Class 5A state championship game as a senior.

He was a preseason All American due to his stellar junior season when he averaged 18 points, 10 rebounds, eight blocks and six assists for Starkville. He was chosen to play in the McDonald's All-Star Game and earned All-State honors all four years in high school in Mississippi along with All-City and All-District honors.

Outlaw is an exceptional leaper and best known for his athleticism. At 6'9, he runs the floor faster than most guards and at the same time is a lethal shot blocker. Outlaw appeared to be staying close to home when he signed with Mississippi State, but has chosen to enter the draft straight out of high school -- following the path taken by Jonathan Bender, the only Mississippian to make the high school-to-NBA leap in 1998.

An early-entry candidate, Hayes is Georgia?s first two-time consensus first-team All-SEC pick since Dominique Wilkins in 1981-82. Hayes was Georgia's top scorer for the past two seasons and it took him just 55 games at Georgia to score 1,000 points -- six games faster than UGA's career scoring leader Litterial Green.

Hayes owns the distinction of scoring titles in two separate leagues: Southeastern Conference in 2002 and the Southern Conference in 2000.

As a junior, Hayes was named honorable mention AP All-American for second straight year and was a consensus first-team All-SEC selection, the only unanimous pick to the coaches' all-league team. Hayes was named one of five "Mid-Season All-Americans" by The Sporting News.

After citing a need to improve his outside shooting from 2002, he delivered in ?03, raising his 3-point percentage from 33 to 43 percent.

After sitting out a year upon transferring from Western Carolina, Hayes was named 2002 SEC Player of the Year by Basketball America, The Sporting News and honorable mention All-America by AP. Hayes was a frst-team All-SEC selection by both AP and the league's 12 coaches, the eighth player in UGA history to win consensus all-league honors. Hayes led the SEC in scoring -- both for the entire season and also for just the 16-game league schedule.

Teams love his toughness, shooting ability and how he gets to the basket. Think a stronger, tougher Emanuel Ginobili.  He's a very good defender, excellent rebounder and an above average athlete.  Seems to have a great understanding of the game.

Delfino doesn't possess the quickness of Ginobili and his shot selection can be a little off.  Relies on his size and athleticism too much on occasion.  Not quite as skilled as some of the other Euros from a fundamental point of view.

Played professionally this past season for Skipper Fortitudo Bologna in the Italian Serie A. Delfino was named Eurobasket All-Europe Youth Players honorable mention in 2002 and was a member of silver-medal winning Argentinean National Team in the 2002 World Championships in Indianapolis. Played this past summer in the Southern California Summer Pro League in Long Beach.

Played for Viola Reggio Calabria (Italy) during the 2001-02 season and was a member of Argentina's bronze-medal winning team at the U-21 World Championships in Japan.

Grew up playing for Libertad Sunchales (Argentina) youth teams and made his debut with Libertad Sunchales during the 1998-99 season. He played the 1999-00 season in the Argentinean minors before moving to Italy for the 2000-01 season, where he was signed by Nuovo Basket Viola Reggio Calabria.

Several teams like Delfino, but a serious ankle injury a month ago really hurt his stock. His agent, David Bauman, claims that there was no ligament damage and plans to bring him to the U.S. for private workouts. He'll have to prove that there isn't any reoccurring problems with the ankle. Can he slip into the first round? He has the talent, but his workouts will be key.

An early-entry candidate, Williams spent just two seasons at Alabama. The SEC freshman of the year in 2002, Williams was named AP third team All-SEC as a sophomore after leading the Tide in scoring (16.4 ppg).

Williams started every game while at Alabama (64 straight) and exited with a 26-point effort against Indiana in the 2003 NCAA Tournament. Williams scored 20 or more points in nine games as a sophomore, including 25 in season opener against Oklahoma and 27 against LSU. He finished the 2002-03 season as the SEC's leader in free throw percentage.

Williams was named to the freshman All-SEC team in 2002 and third team AP All-SEC. He was also the Sporting News National Freshman of the Year, as well as part of the College Insider All-Freshman National Team.

Calderon was an early-entry candidate for the 2002 NBA Draft before withdrawing his name from consideration. He was named to Spain?s National Team that captured fifth place in the 2002 World Championship. Appeared in six games for a total of 39 minutes. Totaled 17 points, four rebounds and four assists.

Professionally, Calderon came up through the ranks of Spain?s lower divisions playing for teams controlled by Tau Ceramica. Loaned to Lucentum Alicante in the LEB for the 1999-2000 season, then stayed on with that team for another season after it was elevated to ACB for 2000-01 season. Switched to Fuenlabrada of the ACB for 2001-02 season, then came home to Tau Ceramica for 2002-03 season.

Barbosa is considered the best player in Brazil. He's very long and an explosive athlete. The thing that has scouts buzzing is the speed at which Barbosa plays for someone his size. He's constantly attacking the basket on offense, and aggressively harassing his man on defense. With his long arms (6-foot-10 wingspan) he gets an unusual amount of steals and blocks for a point guard.

He has an unusual hitch in his outside shot.  He shoots a high percentage in Brazil, but teams are worried that he'll struggle to get it off in the pros.  He can be a little wild at times.  No one has a great handle on the level of competition he's been playing against in Brazil.

How quickly can Barbosa learn English? That's the biggest question in most scout's minds. One Western Conference coach claims that he loves Barbosa, but he's afraid to draft him early because of the language barrier. Your point guard must be able to communicate with the coach and his teammates. His agent has him in English lessons for two hours a day; he better make it four. He could go anwhere from the late lottery to late first round.

A former teammate of Nikoloz Tskitishvili, Pachulia is more of a classic low-post banger. He's strong, likes to mix it up down low and is an excellent rebounder and shot blocker. He's also an above average ball handler for his size.
He's still very raw.  A lack of playing time this season in Turkey hurt his development a bit.  He's not a stiff, but sometimes he looks a little awkward out there.

Teams like the Pacers and Nuggets really liked him when he worked out last year before the draft.  After a slow season in Turkey playing behind the Euroleague MVP, Joe Blair, Pachulia finally got his chance a month ago when Blair went down with an injury. He responded with 26 points on 10 of 13 shooting and added eight rebounds, three assists and three steals in a huge win over defending Euroleague champ Panathinaikos. The game wasn't a fluke. He followed it up with a 13-point, 17-rebound performance against Skipper Bologna. He's probably a late-first-rounder.

One of the most underrated talents in the country, Daniels is productive in virtually every aspect of the game. He played four positions during his Auburn career. A terrific athlete, he displays good change of direction speed and strength lies in going to the basket. Can stop and score from anywhere during the duration of his penetration, because at 6-6, he can shoot over many of the defenders that guard him.

Daniels was named to the All-SEC second team by the Associated Press and SEC coaches after leading the Tigers in four stat categories: averaging 18.4 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 2.3 steals. Daniels was named Auburn's MVP for the third-straight year and led the SEC in steals (2.3), ranked second in scoring, fifth in field goal pct. (.513) and 10th in assists. Daniels was chosen as the SEC?s Most Valuable Player by CollegeInsider.com.

Daniels leaves Auburn as its all-time leader in steals with 208 in his career. He finished ninth on Auburn's career scoring chart with 1,530 points. He averaged 23.3 points, 7.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.3 steals in 35.3 minutes per game in the three NCAA Tournament games, while shooting 53 percent from the field and 33 percent from 3- point range. Daniels scored a game-high 27 points, grabbed a game-high nine rebounds, had four assists and two steals in 38 minutes vs. eventual National Champion Syracuse in the NCAA Tournament Sweet 16.

Pavlovic is a 6-foot-7 swingman who some scouts are comparing to Peja Stojakovic. He's a good mid-range shooter and he's also effective putting the ball on the floor and getting to the basket. He's got great leaping ability and is an above average athlete. Likes to be the "go-to" guy with the game on the line.
He struggles as a defender and has a streaky 3-point shot. He can be too agressive at times.  He needs to get stronger in order to finish more consistently around the basket.

Pavlovic is currently playing for Budcunost in Montenegro and prior to that he was a member of the Serbian Junior National Team. Pavlovic averaged 10 points against Euroleague (24 top teams in Europe) competition during the 2002-03 season.
His stock has been on the rise since Decemeber. He's very confident and, at times, got big time minutes for a Euroleague team. A few strong workouts and he could slip into the late lottery.

Vujacic is a big-time prospect who's stock is beginning to rise dramatically. Vujacic is an athletic combo guard who can play the point or the two. He's great at getting the ball to the basket and has a nice perimeter game to match. He's very smart and sees the floor well.
His defense needs work and he needs to get stronger, but he could be a sleeper to watch.
Currently playing professionally in Italy for Pallalcesto Amatori Udine. Vujacic was a member of Slovenian National Team, which won silver medal at the 2002 European Championship for Young Men.

If he can't get a first-round guarantee, Vujacic will probably pull his name from the draft and wait until next year. But the word around the league is several teams late in the first round are interested.

Jones led Duke in scoring (17.7 ppg) and rebounding (5.5 rpg) as a senior, but defense and athleticism is what he built his reputation on while a Blue Devil. Jones was named first team All-ACC and to the conference's all-defensive team for the second straight year. He was also named to the USBWA All-District III team.

Jones ranked fifth in ACC scoring, sixth in field goal percentage, 11th in free throw shooting and 15th in rebounding. Jones scored in double figures in 31 games as a senior and surpassed 20 points 13 times last season.

Jones was a candidate for national defensive player of the year and a preseason Wooden Award candidate.

Jones transferred to Duke from Rutgers following his sophomore season -- just the second transfer to play for Mike Krzyzewski. Was named to the Big East All-Freshman team (10.7 ppg) while playing for Rutgers. Had an excellent sophomore year (16.0 ppg). Left school and transferred to Duke. Spent the 2000-01 practicing, but not playing with the team as a result of NCAA regulations. Helped lead the U.S. to a gold medal in the 2001 FIBA World Championship for Young Men Tournament over the summer.

Walton has had a disappointing season, thanks in part to reoccurring injuries, and it has caused his stock to slip considerably. Once a lock for the first round, Walton is now being labeled a second-rounder. Still, there is a lot of respect for him in NBA circles. Many consider Walton to be the best passer in the draft, period. Battled multiple ankle injuries his entire senior season, but still managed to earn Honorable Mention All-America honors and was a Wooden Award finalist. Walton was a preseason Associated Press first team All-America pick and was on the preseason and midseason Wooden and Naismith Award watch lists. A Playboy preseason All-America pick as well. Named NABC first team all- District 15. Named all-Pac-10 for the second consecutive season

One of only three players in Pac-10 history to tally 1,000 career points, 500 rebounds and 500 assists. Walton finished his career as the No. 22 career scorer (1,179 points), No. 4 in assists (582), No. 8 in games played (129) and No. 9 in steals (151). An all-NCAA West Regional selection in NCAA Tournament. Averaged 15.5 points, 7.3 rebounds and 7.3 assists in the NCAA Tournament.

Possesses a great all-around game and led all frontcourt players in the country in assists as a junior. Seems to enjoy making everyone around him better due to his understanding of the game.

His 38.4 three-point field goal percentage as a senior was a career best and ranked 10th in the Pac-10 Conference. Comes from a family that has produced its share of basketball talent. Joined his father, Bill, in 2001 as one of only three father-son combinations to play in an NCAA Final Four.

Averaged 13.8 points, 9.8 rebounds and 6.6 assists per game on Arizona?s 10-game tour of Australia following junior season, which saw him named to four All-America teams, as well as the Pac-10 Tournament Most Outstanding Player, after averaging 15.7 points, 7.3 rebounds and 6.3 assists. As a junior, Walton was named one of 10 John R. Wooden Award All-Americans and garnered second team All-America honors from The Sporting News and Basketball News and third team All-America kudos from Basketball Times.

analysis.text:
Cook was named the Big Ten Player of the Year and unanimous first team All-Big Ten by both the media and coaches. He was a third team All-America selection by Associated Press and the Big Ten Tournament Most Outstanding Player. One of 20 finalists for the James Naismith Award and one of 22 finalists for the John Wooden Award , Cook was also a finalist for the USBWA Player of the Year.

Cook ranks third in Illini history in scoring with 1,748 career points and fifth in school history in rebounding with 815 boards. He was the Big Ten scoring champion, finishing league play with a scoring a verage of 20 points and ranked third in the Big Ten in rebounding with an average of 7.6 boards.

As a senior, Cook led Illinois in scoring 22 times and was the Illini's leading rebounder 20 times. Scored at least 15 points in 27 of his 30 games, including 18 games of 20-plus points. Cook recorded eight double-doubles on the season.

Named preseason Big Ten Player of the Year by the media.

analysis.text:
Bell completed his career as Boston College's career scoring leader with 2,632 points. He ranks 21st on the NCAA's all-time career scoring list. Bell also finished as BC's career leader in free throws made (810) and three-point field goals made (300). He was second on the career steals list (272) and third in career scoring average (21.57 ppg).

As a senior this past season, Bell played in and started all 31 games. He averaged 25.2 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 2.3 steals per game. He scored 781 points, setting the school?s single-season record. He was named the Big East Player of the Year for the second time in his career, and captured All-Conference first team honors for the third consecutive year. Bell gained All-America second team honors from the USBWA and ESPN.com., while also earning USBWA District I Player of the Year honors.

In his four seasons, Bell scored 1,388 points in 62 Big East contests -- finishing second on the league's career scoring list and third on its career scoring average list (22.4 ppg). Bell did establish a Big East career record for free throws made (449).

As a freshman, he set the conference scoring record in 1999-2000, averaging 20.1 points per game in 14 league games -- eclipsing the record previously held by former Georgetown star Allen Iverson (19.8 ppg in 1994-95). Bell scored 652 points in 32 games in 2000-01, setting the school record for points by a sophomore.

Bell tallied his 1,000th collegiate point in his 52nd collegiate contest and tallied his 2,000th point in his 98th game -- reaching the milestone in fewer games than any of BC's other three 2,000-point scorers.

Gaines was named a second-team All-America selection by The Sporting News, ESPN.com, and Sports Illustrated, and first team All-America by collegeinsider.com. He also garnered first-team All-Conference USA, USBWA All-District and NABC All-District honors, leading the Cardinals in scoring (17.9, third in C-USA), assists (5.0, 6th in C-USA) and steals (1.7, 7th in C-USA). Also ranked among the league leaders in three point field goal percentage (.389, 11th), assists-to-turnovers ratio (1.67, 10th) and three-point field goals (75, 6th).

Gaines was a finalist for national player of the year awards and was one of 15 finalists for the Oscar Robertson Trophy as the nation's top college basketball player, an award voted on by members of the U.S. Basketball Writers Association. Gaines was one of 20 finalists for the Naismith College Basketball Player of the Year Award, and one of 22 finalists for the John Wooden Award.

Gaines reached double figures in scoring in 31 games as a senior and in 99 games for his career. His 159 assists as a senior was the fifth-highest single-season total ever at Louisville. He finished second in career three-point goals at U of L with 225 (sixth in Conference USA history). Ranks second all-time at U of L in free throws made with 456, the highest career total in Conference USA history.

Korver was a consensus All-American as a senior, including second-team honors from the Associated Press, ESPN.com and the USBWA. A finalist for the Wooden, Naismith and Oscar Robertson National Player of the Year Awards, Korver was named the Missouri Valley Conference's MVP and Valley Tournament MVP. He was also named first-team all-district by the USBWA and NABC, including District Player of the Year honors over Nick Collison and Hollis Price.

One of six players ever to repeat Missouri Valley Conference Player of the Year honors, joining Hersey Hawkins, Xavier McDaniel, Lewis Lloyd, Larry Bird and Junior Bridgeman. Finished his Creighton career fourth all-time in scoring (1,801), first in three-pointers made (371), first in three-point attempts (819), first in three-point accuracy (45.3), first in free throw accuracy (89.1), eighth in assists (294), ninth in blocked shots (58) and fourth in steals (172).

One of the best shooters in NCAA history, Korver owns the Creighton and MVC record with 371 career three-pointers, which is tied for sixth in NCAA history. Also ranks 14th in NCAA history with 45.3-percent accuracy and tops among players 6-7 or taller all-time. As a senior, he was a unanimous choice as collegeinsider.com as Mid-Major National Player of the Year. Set Creighton single-season records for three-pointers made (129), three-point accuracy (.480) and free throw accuracy (.908) while also leading team in scoring (17.8), rebounding (6.4) and steals (1.5).

Korver's 129 treys as a senior in 2002-03 ranks 15th in NCAA single-season history. Ranked among the top 10 nationally in three-pointers made, three-point accuracy and free throw accuracy as a senior. Korver is the only player in Creighton history to appear in four consecutive NCAA Tournaments. Helped lead Creighton to 99 wins in the last four years, easily the best span in school history. Played his best in big games, with seven three-pointers vs. Fresno State and Notre Dame; eight vs. Xavier and five in NCAA Tournament game vs. Central Michigan.

Korver was named MVP of the Guardians Classic after leading Creighton past Notre Dame in Guardians Classic championship game with 24 points and 10 rebounds.

As a junior, led Creighton in scoring (15.1), rebounding (5.5), assists (3.3) and steals (1.6) while earning MVC Player of the Year and honorable-mention All-America honors. As a sophomore, was a second-team all-MVC pick while leading the league champion Jays with 14.6 points per game and hitting a then-record 100 three-pointers while ranking 12th nationally with 45.2 percent accuracy from downtown. As a freshman, he was named to the MVC?s All-Freshman team and All-Newcomer team while averaging 8.8 points per game.

Jason Kapono's four seasons at UCLA included four nods as first team All-Pac-10 -- the first Bruin to accomplish the feat and just the fourth in conference history. Kapono is also the first UCLA player to be named team MVP in four straight seasons and first Bruin to lead the team in scoring in all four seasons.

Kapono was NABC All-District and a preseason candidate for both the Wooden and Naismith awards.

In four seasons, Kapono set a school record for 3-pointers (317) and is second in 3-point FG percentage (44.6). Kapono was the 41st UCLA player to reach 1,000 points in a career and his 2,095 points ranks third in school history. Kapono is tied with former UCLA guard Reggie Miller for seventh all-time in Pac-10 scoring and second in career 3-pointers.

He's another versatile athlete who plays three positions in Europe. He's an excellent outside shooter and possesses a good handle. His ability to get to the basket has improved throughout the year. His experience on the Yugoslavian national team this year was priceless.

He's a little one dimensional. He's not nearly as comfortable putting the ball on the floor and he rarely, if ever, plays with his back to the basket.  For someone so tall, he's just an average rebounder, basically because of his tendency to hang out on the perimeter.  He's not a good defender.

Cabarkapa grew up in Belgrade and began playing at age of 10 with B.C Beopetrol (Yugoslavia). He made his debut in the professional league with B.C Beopetrol during the 1997-98 season and played there until the 2000-01 Championships. He then signed with B.C Buducnost Podgorica for the 2001-02 season and he?s currently still playing there.

Averaged 11.6 points on 47.6-percent shooting for B.C Buducnost Podgorica.

Cabarkapa, 21, has been a member of the Senior Yugoslavian National Team for the last two years. Helped the squad win the gold medal at the 2002 World Championships in Indianapolis. He was the youngest player on the team who played in the World Championships.

Played at the 2000 European Under-20 Championships and was a member of the Yugoslavian University National Team after playing for the Yugoslavian Under-20 National Team. Played in 1999 World University Games.
Given a string of recent strong performances, it's not out of the question that Carbakapa could be the 13th international player selected in the first round this year. He's right there on the bubble.

analysis.text:
Bonner arrived at Gainesville in relative anonymity and left as one of the greatest players ever put on a Florida jersey. He ended his career at Florida ranked eighth on the Gators' all-time scoring list with 1,570 points and finished his career sixth on the school's all-time list for 3-pointers with 165. Bonner is one of only six players in school history with over 1,500 points and over 750 rebounds. The only player in school history with better than 1,500 points, over 750 rebounds and more than 150 3-pointers.

As a senior Bonner earned a spot on the USBWA District IV squad after leading the Gators in scoring with 15.2 ppg and was second in rebounding with 6.1 rpg. For the second straight year, the more important the games got, the better he responded, as he averaged over 16.0 ppg in SEC play for the second straight year. Bonner led the SEC in 3-point shooting, hitting 63-133 (.474). He set career-highs in three-pointers made (63) points (501), assists (49), steals (35), while finishing with over 200 rebounds for the third straight year (201).

Bonner is also one of the most complete student-athletes in college basketball, he was the recipient of the Verizon Academic All-American of the Year for the sport of basketball in both 2002 and 2003. He was also the first Gator basketball player to win the award and only the fourth Gator student-athlete to achieve that honor. In addition, he was a member of the Verizon First Team Academic All-America squad in each of his final three seasons, the first Gator basketball player to do so.

Bonner ended his career as a three-time All-SEC selection, earning first team honors in 2003 (both Coaches and AP), after earning a spot on the second team in 2002 and the third team in 2001.

Sports Illustrated named him one of New Hamsphire's Top 50 Athletes of the Century (No. 12). Bonner graduated first in his high school class (out of 350) and scored 1,350 on his SAT.

Banks is the 31st player in UNLV history to score at least 1,000 points, finishing his career with 1,139 to put him at 24th on the all-time UNLV list. He is only the ninth player in UNLV history to score 1,000 points in his first two seasons in a Runnin? Rebel uniform. He ranks fifth in career points for players who only played only two seasons at UNLV.

As a senior, Banks led the Runnin' Rebels in scoring (20.3 ppg), assists (5.5 apg) and steals (2.8 spg) earned honorable mention All-America by AP. He was named USBWA District 8 Player of the Year and was a member of the 10-player All-District 8 team. Banks was selected first team All-MWC and MWC co-Defensive Player of the Year. He was also named to the MWC All-Tournament team.

Banks, who transfered from Dixie College in St. George, Utah, ranks sixth on the UNLV all-time career steals list with 158 and second all-time in a single season at UNLV with 91 in 2002-03. Banks scored in double figures in 51 games for his career, scored 20 or more points in a game 27 times and 30 or more in a game eight times.

analysis.text:
An early-entry candidate, Powell was a first-team All-ACC Tournament selection as a sophomore after averaging 20 points, seven rebounds and three blocks in the Pack's run to the title game. On the season, Powell ranked 12th in the ACC in free throw percentage (.739) and sixth in blocked shots with 1.32 a game.

As a freshman, Powell was named to the ACC?s All-Rookie team after leading N.C. State in blocked shots with 30. Powell was named to the ACC Honor Roll his freshman year, as he posted a 3.45 grade point average.

Hansen was named first team All-MWC and the MWC co-defensive player of the year. Hansen led BYU in scoring as both a senior and junior (16.8 ppg and 15.6 ppg). As a senior, he led the Cougars in blocks (20), and was second in rebounds (4.8) and assists (2.4). Also led BYU in rebounds (6.2) as a junior.

Hansen leaves BYU as the school's 24th career scorer with 1,137 points in two-plus seasons. Made 71 starts in 86 games. Career highs of 30 points and 17 rebounds. His 17 boards at Pepperdine is the most ever by a BYU guard and the most by any Cougar since in 1983. At the 2003 Portsmouth Invitational, averaged 15.7 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists, shooting 19-33 (.576), 5-8 (.625) on NBA threes, and 4-5 (.800) on free throws. Named to the Portsmouth All-Tournament Team and received event?s Sportsmanship Award.

Hansen was one of two consensus All-MWC first team picks and NABC Division I All-District 13 First Team and USBWA District 8 Team. Scored double figures a team-leading 30 times. Led BYU in scoring 18 times, including the 11 of the last 15 games. He reached 20 points for the ninth time with a team-leading 21 vs. UConn in the NCAA Tournament. Had 12 boards, scored 21 points, making a career-best 14 free throws on 15 attempts  vs. Utah while recording his second double-double.

Following his senior season, Bogans was named second-team All-America by the NABC and third-team by The Associated Press. Bogans was also named SEC Player of the Year by the league?s coaches, while also earning first-team All-SEC honors by the AP and Coaches.

Bogans played in all 36 games with 35 starts, averaging a team-high 15.7 ppg for the 32-4 Wildcats. He shot a career-best 38.3 percent from 3-point range and finished second on the team in assists with 2.7 apg. Finished his UK career with 1,923 points, which ranks fourth on school's all-time scoring list. Bogans also totaled 314 career assists, ranking 12th at UK. He ranks second at UK in career 3s made (254) and first in 3-point attempts (743).

Bogans was named MVP of the SEC Tournament after averaging 17.0 points. On the season, he ranked second in the league in FT percentage (SEC games) 84.4 percent

analysis.text:
Arguably the top Division II player in the country the past two seasons, Beasley was once again named the Division II Bulletin and Daktronics NCAA Division II player of the year after leading UND in scoring (26.6 ppg) and rebounding (8.9 rpg). He was also the North Central Conference's MVP for the second consecutive season, shooting 51.3 percent from the field and 45.8 percent from behind the 3-point arc.

Beasley scored a career high 41 points against Augustana and ending his college career with a 37-point effort against St. Cloud State in the NCAA Division II North Central Region tournament. Beasley finished with 1,402 points in two seasons at North Dakota, reaching the 1,000-point milestone quicker than any player in school history (45 games). His 772 points as a senior is the second-most by any Sioux player in the school's 99-year history. He finished 10th on the school's all-time scoring list, despite playing just two seasons after transferring from Midland JC in Texas.

Blake was a first team All-ACC choice who was a finalist for the Wooden Award and Naismith National Player of the Year Award. As a senior, Blake was easily the most experienced point guard in the nation -- he finished fifth on the NCAA?s all-time assists chart with 972 -- 28 from becoming the fourth Division I player in history with 1,000 assists. He leaves Maryland No. 4 all-time in assists in ACC history behind Bobby Hurley (1,076), Chris Corchiani (1,038) and Ed Cota (1,030).

Blake set a Maryland record for career starts (136). Is 39th player in Maryland history to score 1,000 points. He became the first player in ACC history with 1,000 points, 800 assists, 400 rebounds and 200 steals. Blake joined UNC?s Ed Cota as just the second player in ACC history with 1,000 points, 800 assists and 400 rebounds.

He ranks third on Maryland?s career chart for 3FGs (182) and is one of just four players in Maryland history with over 200 career steals, fourth (234) behindJohnny Rhodes (344), Juan Dixon (333) and Laron Profit (252). Blake played in every game of his college career: 138 games, 136 starts during a four-year career which includes two trips to the Final Four, a national title and 15 NCAA Tournament games. Maryland was 103-35 with Blake as its point guard overall, 13-3 in the NCAA Tournament. Blake was part of 51 career ACC victories.

As a junior, Blake was the Terrapin's floor leader who achieved honorable mention All-America, third team All-ACC, honorable mention All-ACC Defensive team and second team ACC All-Tournament honors. Established a Maryland single-season record with 286 assists, the fifth-best total in ACC history. He led the ACC in assists for the second straight season (7.9) and finished his junior year with more more assists through three seasons than any player in ACC history besides Bobby Hurley (814).

Nicknamed Baby Shaq by his teammates in Greece, he's very strong and capable of playing with his back to the basket. He's a good rebounder and can score in the low post. He has a nice array of post moves including a sweet baby hook. He can be very agressive, but somehow his game looks smooth.

His stock has dropped lately as teams question his size. His agent, Marc Fleisher, claims that he was recently measured at 6-10, 287 with shoes. Will that stop the slippage? It's tough to call. He's not a great athlete and doesn't have much of a face the basket game.  He's probably a center trapped in a power forward's body. Like Shaq he's a terrible free throw shooter.

An early-entry candidate, he made his first full season in the Greek League with Iraklis after making his debut as a professional at the age of 15. Ranked in the top 10 in field goal shooting (58.3 percent) and average 6.2 rebounds. Played for the Greek national team in 2001, averaging 10.1 rebounds.

There's only so much demand for physical, undersized power forwards in the league. Workouts will be big for him. If he projects to be like Elton Brand, he'll move way up this chart. If he's closer to Danny Fortson, then the mid-to-late first round is just about right.

analysis.text:
Ross leaves SMU as its No. 4 all-time scorer with 1,761 points. The two-time all-WAC selection led the WAC in scoring as a senior at 20.3 points a game. He also ranked among the leaders in rebounds (6.4 rpg), FT percentage (79.3), steals (46) and blocks (24).

Ross ranks among SMU?s career leaders in multiple categories -- scoring (4th), field goals made (8th) and attempted (6th), 3-pointers made (3rd) and attempted (3rd); free throws made (3rd) and attempted (4th); steals (6th) and blocks (6th).

Ross recorded 91 career games in double-figures, 31 20-plus point performances and nine double-doubles in his career.

Hunter was a first-team all-MAC selection for the third straight season and an All-Midwest selection by Basketball Times. Hunter was named to the Wooden Award Watch list as a preseason All-America choice and became one of three players in MAC history to score 2,000 points and grab 1,000 rebounds in a career (2,012/1,103).

Hunter was named MAC East Division Player of the Week four times, more than anyone else in the league. He led the Bobcats in scoring (21.5 ppg) and blocked shots (35), while also leading the nation in double-doubles through regular season (23). Hunter posted a double-double in 11 straight games at one point, the longest streak in the country all year. He also topped double figures in scoring every contest. Enjoyed his best offensive day at Marshall, tallying 35 points (27 of which came after intermission). He also hit for 33 against Ball State, 32 at Buffalo and 30 against Akron in two meetings.

analysis.text: He's a 6-foot-6 point guard with a solid outside shot and excellent court vision.  He's a pretty good athlete and runs the floor very well. He's unselfish, sometimes to a fault.  A very intelligent player that really understands the game.

Planinic appears to be a bit on the frail side. He's going to have to hit the weight room before he steps onto an NBA court. He can be a little passive at times.  He won't be the vocal leader some teams look for in a point guard.

Planinic is currently playing for Cibona, the Croatian League champions, in Zagreb, Croatia. At the age of 19, Planinic was named the MVP of the Euroleague Opening Tournament, leading his team to victories over Maccabi Tel Aviv, Panathinaikos, and Kinder Bologna. Planinic is considered the top pure point guard in Europe. He is very quick and versatile and has a great all-around game.

Planinic played for the 2003 Croatian National Team that qualified for the 2003 European Championships, which will be played this September in Sweeden. Planinic was named the 2001-02 Best Croatian Young Player.

At the beginning of the year, some teams had him pegged as a lottery pick. An early-season car wreck injury really hurt his season. He never really rebounded and his stock has really dropped. But, remember, teams will always take a risk on a 6-6 point guard. Should be an early second rounder.

Green was the 2003 Horizon League Player of the Year and the league's top scorer. He finished his college career as the fourth-leading scorer in Detroit history (1,779 points). Green was chosen as a Mid-Major All-American by collegeinsider.com, as well as first-team all-conference.

Green leaves Detroit as its sixth-leading career 3-pointer shooter with 120 treys. He was a four-year starter at UDM, scoring at least 20 points in 31 games as a Titan (19 times last season alone).

As a senior, Green led the conference in scoring with a 22.6 average (ranked 11th nationally), and his 678 points as a senior represents the ninth-highest one-year total in Detroit history. He was named to the Horizon League all-tournament team after averaging 25.7 points in postseason tourney games against Wright State, Loyola and Butler.

analysis.text: He's huge. At 7-foot-6 he would be the second tallest player in the NBA behind only Shawn Bradley. The good news is that he isn't a stiff. He can run the floor, block shots and has enough meat on him to defend in the league.
The bad news ... he's very raw offensively and defensively.  He's struggled to get in the game in Yugoslavia -- that's not easy to do when you're that size.
The 20-year-old Vranes is currently playing for Budcunost in Montenegro and prior to that he was a member of FMP Zeleznik Beograd junior team.
He's not ready for the NBA but that doesn't mean that NBA teams won't take a shot on him in the late first round. In the NBA, size really does matter.

analysis.text:
Douglas enjoyed one of the most prolific offensive seasons in school history, leading all Division I scorers in 2002-03, averaging 28.0 point a game. He was named the 2003 Mountain West Conference Player of the Year and honorable mention AP All-American. He was also selected all-district by the USBWA and NABC.

Douglas finished fifth all-time in New Mexico scoring with 1,782 points in less than three full seasons. He was only 211 points off the all-time career mark of 1,993 set by Charles Smith over four years (1994-97). His 783 points as a senior is the second best single-season total at UNM. He was just one point shy of Kenny Page?s record set in 1980.

Douglas became the MWC's career scoring leader with 1,782 points. Douglas was a midseason transfer from the University of Arizona who made his Lobo debut Dec. 21, 2000.

Dupree finished his LSU career with 1,726 points, which ranks No. 8 all-time at the school. His 907 career rebounds rank sixth all-time at the school. Dupree is also just one of four players -- joining Shaquille O?Neal, Durand Macklin and Bob Pettit -- to finish in the top 10 in both scoring and rebounding in their LSU careers.

Dupree averaged 16.5 points in the 16 SEC games, fifth in the league, and his 8.3 rebounds tied for second. Overall, his 15.8 points per game average was seventh best in the league and his rebound average of 7.8 was fourth. Dupree had his third consecutive 500 point season, scoring 504 points as a senior. Field goal percentage of 52.9 percent (199-of-376) was third in the league and the best of his career. Dupree had the longest consecutive double-figure scoring string in his career with 29 games. He recorded eight games of 20 or more points during the season and tallied 25 games of 20 or more points in his career.
